subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: One assignment on set or wider-reading texts

questions.q: How many assignments does a candidate submit for Component 5 (Coursework) in Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English (0475)?
options: One assignment
Two assignments
Three assignments
Four assignments
questions.explain: Component 5 requires candidates to submit a single piece of coursework.

questions.q: What percentage of the total qualification does Component 5 (Coursework) carry?
questions.explain: The coursework component is weighted at 25% of the overall qualification.

questions.q: Approximately how long should the coursework assignment be?
options: About 500 words
About 1000 words
About 2000 words
About 5000 words
questions.explain: The single assignment should be around 2000 words in length.

questions.q: Out of how many marks is the coursework assignment assessed?
options: 10 marks
25 marks
40 marks
50 marks
questions.explain: The assignment is marked out of 25, using the coursework assessment criteria.

questions.q: How is Component 5 coursework assessed?
options: Marked internally by the centre and externally moderated by Cambridge
Marked entirely by Cambridge examiners under exam conditions
Peer-marked by other candidates in the class
Marked only by the candidate as self-assessment
questions.explain: Coursework is internally marked by the teaching centre and then externally moderated by Cambridge.

questions.q: The coursework assignment may be based on which of the following?
options: A set text or a text chosen from wider reading
Only a Shakespeare play
Only unseen poetry
Only a text studied for another subject
questions.explain: The assignment can be written on a set text or on a suitable text from wider reading.

questions.q: Which quality is central to a strong coursework response?
options: An informed personal response to the text
Memorised biographical facts about the author
A word-for-word retelling of the plot
Agreement with a published critic's view
questions.explain: Candidates are expected to communicate an informed, personal response to the literature.

questions.q: Analysis in the coursework assignment should focus mainly on which aspects of a text?
options: The writer's use of language, structure and form
The number of pages and chapters
The publication date and price
The author's other unrelated works
questions.explain: Effective analysis explores how a writer uses language, structure and form to shape meaning.

questions.q: Why is choosing an appropriate text important for the coursework assignment?
options: It allows sustained, detailed analysis and a developed personal response
It guarantees a longer word count without effort
It removes the need to quote from the text
It means the candidate can avoid analysis
questions.explain: A suitable text gives enough substance for the candidate to analyse in depth and respond personally.

questions.q: What does a 'personal response' to a text mean in this context?
options: The candidate's own informed interpretation, supported by textual evidence
An emotional reaction with no reference to the text
A summary of what teachers said in class
A comparison with the candidate's personal diary
questions.explain: A personal response is the candidate's own considered view, grounded in evidence from the text.

questions.q: Which of the following best demonstrates analysis rather than mere description?
options: Explaining how a metaphor conveys a character's inner conflict
Listing the main events of the plot in order
Stating how many characters appear in the story
Copying out a long quotation without comment
questions.explain: Analysis explores how the writer's techniques create meaning and effect, not just what happens.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of external moderation of coursework?
options: To ensure marking standards are applied consistently across all centres
To rewrite candidates' assignments for them
To choose which texts candidates must study
To replace internal marking entirely
questions.explain: Moderation checks that centres have applied the assessment criteria to a common standard.

questions.q: What is meant by a 'wider-reading' text for the assignment?
options: A suitable literary text beyond the set texts, chosen for study
Any non-fiction textbook from another subject
A text that has not been read at all
A summary website about a novel
questions.explain: Wider reading refers to appropriate literary texts studied in addition to the set texts.

questions.q: How can a candidate best support their personal response in the assignment?
options: By using close reference to and quotation from the text
By restating the essay title several times
By writing at greater length without evidence
By describing the book's cover design
questions.explain: Well-chosen references and quotations give a personal response credibility and depth.

questions.q: How does coursework differ from a timed examination response?
options: It is produced over time, allowing drafting and redrafting
It must be handwritten in one hour
It cannot include any quotations
It is marked without any criteria
questions.explain: Coursework is developed over time rather than written under timed exam conditions.

questions.q: A candidate's draft is mostly plot summary with no comment on the writing. What should they add to improve it?
options: Their own analysis and personal interpretation of the writer's choices
More detail about the sequence of events
A list of every character's name
The exact page numbers of each scene
questions.explain: Adding analysis and personal response moves the work beyond summary to critical engagement.

questions.q: A candidate wants to write the assignment on a novel that is not on the set-text list. Is this acceptable?
options: Yes, provided it is a suitable literary text from wider reading
No, only set texts are ever allowed
Yes, but only if it is a poem
No, unless it is studied for a different subject
questions.explain: The assignment may be based on a set text or an appropriate wider-reading text.

questions.q: A candidate frequently quotes the text but never explains the quotations. What is the best improvement?
options: Analyse how the writer's choices create meaning and effect
Include more quotations of greater length
Remove all quotations from the assignment
Add a summary of the plot instead
questions.explain: Quotations must be analysed to show how the writer shapes meaning, not simply inserted.

questions.q: A candidate submits a coursework assignment of around 4000 words. Why might a teacher advise revising it?
options: It greatly exceeds the recommended length of about 2000 words
Coursework must be under 500 words
Longer work automatically scores higher marks
There is no recommended length to consider
questions.explain: The assignment should be about 2000 words, so a much longer piece would need trimming.

questions.q: A centre wants to be sure its internal marks are fair before Cambridge sees them. What process addresses this?
options: Applying the assessment criteria consistently, ready for external moderation
Asking candidates to mark their own work
Awarding every candidate full marks
Ignoring the criteria and marking by impression
questions.explain: Consistent internal marking against the criteria is what external moderation then verifies.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English (0475) syllabus; Component 5: Coursework
